experiment_description: Central concept: the work requires an intense nonclassical driving field, bright squeezed vacuum (BSV), with vanishing mean electric field and strong intensity fluctuations, to test whether quantum-light fluctuations can act as a coherence filter in xenon strong-field photoelectron holography. The source-generation procedure uses type-I spontaneous parametric down-conversion in a collinear, frequency-degenerate geometry. An amplified Ti:sapphire femtosecond laser at 800 nm central wavelength, 25 fs pulse duration, 3 kHz repetition rate, and tunable single-pulse energy up to about 700 µJ pumps a pair of 2-mm-thick beta-barium borate (BBO) crystals placed symmetrically about the common focus of an f = 1000 mm lens. The BBO crystals are angularly tuned for degenerate phase matching near 1600 nm. A long-pass filter with 1180 nm cutoff removes residual 800 nm pump light after the crystal pair, and an f = 600 mm lens collimates the down-converted beam. The goal is to determine whether this double-crystal high-gain SPDC recipe produces an intense degenerate BSV beam suitable for strong-field ionization, with the output energy measured after pump rejection and collimation. The relevant spatial scope is the full collinear BSV beam emerging from the crystal pair and collimation optics; no spatial beam-profile map is reported in the text.

bsv_generation_of_intense_degenerate_pul.description: Whether the specified double-crystal high-gain SPDC procedure produced the intended intense degenerate BSV pulse source.

maximum_bsv_average_pulse_energy_uJ.description: The maximum reported average pulse energy of the generated BSV source after the specified generation and filtering procedure.

experiment_description: Central concept: the strong-field ionization experiment is designed around BSV as a quantum light state with super-Poissonian photon-number fluctuations, so the photon statistics and spectral mode content of the BSV source must be characterized before interpreting xenon photoelectron interference as a quantum-noise-filtered process. Immediately after BSV generation by the double-BBO type-I SPDC source pumped at 800 nm, a low-reflectivity glass plate samples a small fraction of the collimated BSV beam. The pickoff is sent to Spectrometer-1, an AvaSpec-NIR256-2.5-HSC-EVO covering 1000–2500 nm. For each laser shot the spectrum I(λ) is recorded; after accounting for the spectrometer response S(λ) and the glass-plate reflection coefficient R, the pulse photon number is computed as N = (1/R)∫dλ I(λ)/S(λ). For each BSV intensity setting corresponding to the ionization measurements, spectra from 20,000 consecutive pulses are recorded over the whole sampled beam accepted by the spectrometer. The second-order intensity correlation is evaluated in the large-photon-number limit as g^(2) = <N^2>/<N>^2. The same shot ensemble is used for spectral Schmidt-mode analysis: the wavelength–wavelength intensity-fluctuation covariance Cov(λ,λ′)=<ΔI(λ)ΔI(λ′)> is normalized to a dimensionless correlation kernel C(λ,λ′), its matrix square root K=sqrt(C) is singular-value-decomposed as K(λ,λ′)=Σ_m s_m u_m(λ)u_m*(λ′), giving orthonormal spectral modes u_m and weights s_m. For evaluating which modes contribute to xenon ionization, each mode weight is multiplied by the ADK tunnel-ionization rate. The independent BSV pulse-energy conditions are 3.3, 5.0, 8.3, and 10 µJ average pulse energy, matching the later COLTRIMS measurements.

g2_at_3p3_uJ_dimensionless.description: The measured second-order intensity correlation of the BSV photon-number distribution for the lowest pulse-energy condition.

g2_at_5p0_uJ_dimensionless.description: The measured second-order intensity correlation of the BSV photon-number distribution for the second pulse-energy condition.

g2_at_8p3_uJ_dimensionless.description: The measured second-order intensity correlation of the BSV photon-number distribution for the third pulse-energy condition.

g2_at_10_uJ_dimensionless.description: The measured second-order intensity correlation of the BSV photon-number distribution for the highest pulse-energy condition.

first_schmidt_mode_dominates_bsv_spectra.description: Whether the spectral Schmidt decomposition identifies the first spectral mode as the dominant mode of the measured BSV ensemble.

higher_schmidt_modes_ionization_contribu.description: Upper bound on the fraction of xenon ionization events attributed to Schmidt modes beyond the first when modal weights are combined with ADK ionization rates for the highest BSV intensity condition.

experiment_description: Central concept: the BSV pulse duration determines the ultrafast strong-field interaction window in which xenon electron trajectories experience quantum-light fluctuations, so the temporal envelope of the generated BSV beam is characterized independently. The collimated BSV beam from the double-BBO SPDC source is redirected into a frequency-resolved optical gating (FROG) apparatus using a flipping mirror. A polarizing beam splitter divides the beam into two orthogonal components that propagate through two arms; a delay stage scans the relative delay over the recorded FROG time window. The two arms are recombined at a second polarizing beam splitter and focused into a BBO crystal for second-harmonic generation. The SHG spectrum is recorded versus delay, producing a time–wavelength spectrogram over the plotted SHG wavelength interval of roughly 700–850 nm and delay interval of roughly 0–150 fs. A standard FROG retrieval algorithm reconstructs the temporal intensity envelope at the input of the interaction region, and the pulse duration is extracted as the full width at half maximum of that retrieved envelope. The spatial scope is the BSV beam mode coupled into the FROG apparatus; no transverse-resolved pulse-duration map is reported.

bsv_pulse_duration_fwhm_fs.description: The FWHM duration of the retrieved BSV temporal intensity envelope at the input of the interaction region.

experiment_description: Central concept: xenon strong-field ionization driven by BSV tests whether a nonclassical, zero-mean, strongly fluctuating optical field suppresses phase-sensitive above-threshold-ionization structures while preserving dynamically correlated photoelectron-holography pathways. BSV pulses generated by type-I degenerate SPDC near 1600 nm are focused by a 75 mm focal-length concave mirror into a pulsed supersonic xenon gas jet inside a COLTRIMS reaction microscope held at 5×10^-11 mbar. The xenon backing pressure is 0.7 atm, chosen to provide ionization yield while avoiding space-charge effects. Four BSV average pulse-energy conditions are used: 3.3, 5.0, 8.3, and 10 µJ, corresponding to average peak intensities of 0.53×10^14, 0.80×10^14, 1.33×10^14, and 1.60×10^14 W/cm^2. The BSV photon statistics are the characterized super-Poissonian distributions for these energy conditions. Electrons from the xenon target are extracted and guided by calibrated electric and magnetic fields to a microchannel-plate detector with a delay-line detector, giving time- and position-resolved single-electron detection. Millions of events are accumulated for each optical condition to reconstruct three-dimensional electron momenta. The reported momentum-distribution scope includes two-dimensional projections in p_x versus p_z over approximately p_x = -0.4 to 0.4 a.u. and p_z = -0.6 to 0.6 a.u., and cylindrical projections p_r = sqrt(p_x^2+p_y^2) versus p_z over approximately p_r = 0 to 1 a.u. and p_z = -0.6 to 0.6 a.u. The measurement targets interference features associated with direct, indirect, and forward-scattered subcycle electron trajectories in the focal-volume overlap of the gas jet and BSV beam; no spatially resolved target-volume map is reported.

bsv_driven_ati_peak_visibility.description: The visibility category of above-threshold-ionization peak/ring features in xenon PMDs under BSV driving across the measured pulse-energy conditions.

bsv_driven_spider_holographic_fringe_det.description: Whether spider-like photoelectron-holography fringes associated with indirect and forward-scattered electron trajectory interference are detected in the BSV-driven xenon PMDs across the measured conditions.

bsv_driven_non_spider_interference_visib.description: The visibility category of competing non-spider photoelectron interference structures in xenon PMDs under BSV driving.

bsv_driven_dominant_surviving_interferen.description: The trajectory-pair channel identified from the measured BSV-driven PMD morphology as the surviving holographic interference contribution.

experiment_description: Central concept: a coherent-state reference at the same mid-infrared wavelength provides the classical-field baseline for determining which xenon photoelectron-interference features are selectively filtered by BSV quantum fluctuations. In the COLTRIMS apparatus, the BSV beam is replaced by coherent-state mid-infrared pulses at 1600 nm generated by an optical parametric amplifier pumped by the same Ti:sapphire laser system. The coherent-state output is routed through the same optical path and focused into the same pulsed supersonic xenon gas jet with the same 75 mm focal-length concave mirror and target geometry used for BSV measurements. The chamber pressure is 5×10^-11 mbar, and the xenon backing pressure is 0.7 atm. The coherent-state peak intensity condition is 1.0×10^14 W/cm^2. Electrons are extracted and guided with calibrated electric and magnetic fields to an MCP plus delay-line detector for time- and position-resolved single-event measurement, with millions of events accumulated to reconstruct three-dimensional momenta. The reported reference PMD is plotted as p_r = sqrt(p_x^2+p_y^2) versus p_z over approximately p_r = 0 to 1 a.u. and p_z = -0.6 to 0.6 a.u. The reference photon-number distribution is characterized with the same large-photon-number convention g^(2)=<N^2>/<N>^2. The measurement targets ATI rings and trajectory-pair interference features in the full gas-jet/focal-volume overlap; no spatially resolved target-volume map is reported.

coherent_state_g2_dimensionless.description: The measured second-order intensity correlation of the coherent-state reference pulses used for xenon ionization.

coherent_driven_ati_ring_visibility.description: The visibility category of above-threshold-ionization ring features in the coherent-state-driven xenon PMD.

coherent_driven_carpet_interference_visi.description: The visibility category of carpet-like photoelectron interference structures in the coherent-state-driven xenon PMD.
